claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a native, thin oxide scale.
Controlled post-deposition annealing will thicken the oxide layer on the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Controlled post-deposition annealing will stabilize the oxide layer on the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The annealed coating will have a more adherent oxide layer than the as-deposited coating.
A thicker oxide layer acts as a mechanical barrier during sliding.
The thicker oxide layer reduces direct metal-to-metal contact.
The thicker oxide layer redistributes contact stresses.
The thicker oxide layer mitigates local stress concentrations at the sliding interface.
Mitigation of direct contact and local stress concentrations reduces adhesive and abrasive wear.
Mitigation of local stress concentrations reduces plastic deformation during sliding.
Annealed coatings with enhanced oxide layers will have a lower wear rate than as-deposited coatings during high-temperature sliding.
Annealed coatings with enhanced oxide layers will exhibit less microscopic plastic flow than as-deposited coatings.
Annealed coatings with enhanced oxide layers will exhibit less micro-cracking than as-deposited coatings.
The predicted oxide-mediated improvements hold above approximately 300°C under oxidizing sliding conditions.
The oxide-mediated mechanism will be less influential at lower temperatures or in inert atmospheres.
Prior studies on similar coatings indicate beneficial effects from controlled oxide formation.
Oxide adhesion, annealing-induced microstructural evolution, and sliding-contact conditions may influence wear and microscopic deformation.
